key_insight: EP-Flow predicts disordered crystal structures from chemical formulas by modeling site occupancies as a constrained occupancy distribution matrix instead of requiring site-level disorder labels.
engineering_relevance: It enables practical discovery of functional disordered materials such as solid solutions, vacancy-rich phases, and interstitially occupied crystals when only composition is known.
method: Defines an Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM) to unify ordered and disordered crystals in one continuous representation.
Uses Entropic Polytope Flow to map heterogeneous formula-dependent constraint polytopes into a shared double-centered space.
Recovers feasible occupancies with a Sinkhorn inverse map while jointly generating occupancies, fractional coordinates, and lattice parameters.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art results on formula-conditioned disordered crystal structure prediction benchmarks derived from COD and MPDS, with better performance than adapted ordered-crystal generators.
watch_item: Performance depends on solving constrained transport-like inference, so feasibility and numerical stability of the Sinkhorn-based inverse map may be a practical implementation concern.
paper_title: EP-Flow: Disordered Crystal Structure Prediction without Site-Level Annotations
